name: Eurasianism
summary: Eurasianism holds that Russia and its neighbouring lands form a distinct civilisation between Europe and Asia, to be united in a Eurasian state or union and set against Western, liberal universalism. Classical Eurasianists of the 1920s favoured an authoritarian, Orthodox-inflected ideocratic state and a Slavic-Turkic symbiosis, while neo-Eurasianism adds geopolitical opposition to the Atlantic bloc, a strong state and traditionalism.
scope: Classical Eurasianism of Trubetskoy, Savitsky, Florovsky and Alekseev, together with the neo-Eurasianism of Aleksandr Dugin, which is the version in current use. Where they differ, answers follow what both share (anti-West, empire, civilisational unity, strong state, religion). Economic and many social answers are inferred with low confidence.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism opposes Atlantic economic penetration and favours a state-directed strong economy, so blocking foreign takeovers is inferred as agreed.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The Orthodox-inflected, traditionalist outlook tells against easy divorce; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Eurasianists favoured an authoritarian, ideocratic state and criticised Western liberal democracy, so instructed and recallable delegates is inferred as opposed.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The state-directed, strong-state economic outlook favours state-run provision over private accounts; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Eurasianists did not set a land tenure doctrine; a state-guided economy and private holdings both fit, so inferred as split.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Eurasianism prefers a strong, ideocratic executive over a liberal parliament, so parliamentary budget approval as a condition is inferred as disfavoured.

single-official-language.rationale: Eurasianism praises a multi-ethnic Slavic-Turkic union, so restricting other languages for one sole language is inferred as disfavoured.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism treats national land as sovereign civilisational territory against Atlantic influence; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Dugin rejects Western universalist liberal norms, which include outcome-based anti-discrimination; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Eurasianism sets traditional and spiritual values against Western materialist consumer culture; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Foundations of Geopolitics advocates destabilising Atlanticist states and supporting separatist and opposition movements; inferred as agreed.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Eurasianism sees a Russia-led Eurasian bloc and its empire as a unity to be held together, so intervention to keep members in the bloc is inferred as agreed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Opposes Western liberal markets in favour of a state-directed economy; influence of private corporations is inferred as unwelcome.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Central opposition to Western influence and Atlanticism implies restricting foreign-funded NGOs, media and universities in the Eurasian space.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Traditionalism and a strong civilisational state imply support for family and birth-rate policy; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Sovereignty and rootedness in place are stressed; limiting property to locals is inferred rather than stated.

job-guarantee.rationale: A statist third-way economy under a strong state implies state responsibility for employment; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Rejects liberal universalism and Western democracy promotion as a form of Atlantic hegemony.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Favours an authoritarian ideocratic state with obedience to the national idea; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Opposes Western intervention but claims a Russian sphere of influence over neighbouring lands, so a universal ban is not held.

industrial-unions.rationale: Economic organisation of labour was not a focus; no stance can be inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Classical Eurasianism stressed Slavic-Turkic symbiosis and a multi-ethnic civilisation; Atlanticist conspiracy talk is not aimed at a minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Traditionalism and Orthodox-inflected values imply keeping marriage as a legal institution; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: An authoritarian ideocratic state is unlikely to endorse a legal right to government information; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Opposes globalisation and favours autarky of large economic spaces, though not strictly local production; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The ideocratic state is led by an organised elite and movement, opposite to informal leaderless groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Rejects Western-dominated international law and universal human-rights norms in favour of civilisational sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: Orthodoxy is given a central role in the Russian national state, though Eurasia is conceived as multi-confessional.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not directly addressed; Eurasianists want a Russian-led union but insist on equality of civilisations, so adherents are split on ritual deference.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from the call for a strong centralised Eurasian state rather than regional autonomy over revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not addressed; Dugin's third-way economy leaves the personal/productive line unspecified.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: neo-Eurasianism is hostile to liberal capitalism more than to Soviet-style statism, and Dugin has National Bolshevik sympathies.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a statist but non-doctrinaire third-way economy.

religion-illusion.rationale: Orthodoxy and traditional religion are central to Eurasianism, which holds that religion is a lasting foundation of civilisation.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Eurasianists reject Western liberal modernity and its market society as a model for Russia and the world.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from Dugin's traditionalist stress on family and gender roles.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist emphasis on the family as a basic unit.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents have no clear doctrine on language purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the imperial, centralising model under which the state ultimately decides.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: the model is a unified Eurasian state or empire, not many small communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Classical Eurasianists favoured a Slavic-Turkic symbiosis, but the neo-Eurasian empire involves Russian leadership; adherents split.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Dugin's Fourth Political Theory rejects liberalism, communism and fascism alike and Eurasianism claims a distinct third path.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Eurasianism rests on the idea of a Eurasian space bound to its peoples by history, and neo-Eurasianism uses it to justify claims over neighbouring lands.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred rejection, though some in the wider milieu flirt with revisionism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Dugin's traditionalism is hostile to homosexuality and sympathetic to criminal or legal bans; inferred from his traditionalism, with classical Eurasianists silent.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Classical Eurasianists favoured an authoritarian single-ideology (ideocratic) state, and neo-Eurasianism a strong state.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The ideocratic state was Orthodox-inflected and Eurasianists gave the Church a national role, so legal protection of the faith follows.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Eurasianists present empire as a symbiosis of peoples rather than exploitation, though they back imperial rule; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A specifically Islamic obligation; Eurasianism treats Islam as a partner but takes no position on this.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: They favour religiously grounded states but no source endorses removing rulers by force over religious law; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: They denounce liberal democracy while Dugin uses participatory language for a corporate and ethnic order, so adherents are split; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism is militantly opposed to Western progressive identity politics; inferred from its anti-liberalism.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Dugin's traditionalism rejects Western gender liberalisation; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Orthodox-inflected traditionalism.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Eurasianism presents itself as a third position beyond liberalism, communism and fascism, combining elements of right and left.

alienated-labor.rationale: Anti-capitalist but not in Marxian terms; the idea was not addressed and adherents would be split.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Eurasianism builds on a Slavic-Turkic symbiosis and treats Islam as part of Eurasian civilisation, not as alien to it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The classical ideocratic state drew on Orthodox religion and Eurasianists stress the Church's role in the national state.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: They favour a role for religion in public life, so bans on religious dress are inferred to be disfavoured.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A modern employment-law matter outside the doctrine; no position inferable.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic views are a vague statist third way between liberal capitalism and socialism, so adherents are split on this specific model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism is built on great-power geopolitics and military strength against the Atlantic bloc.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; state-directed economic views leave adherents split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Eurasianism is itself a rival bloc strategy, with Russia leading a Eurasian union against the Atlantic bloc.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from the classical ideocratic state ruled by a selected elite rather than a dynasty; not discussed directly.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed; neo-Eurasianism favours a state-directed third-way economy without a stated view on cooperative credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from the opposition to Western liberal institutions and the Atlantic bloc, though lenders as such were not addressed.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred from the ideocratic selection of a ruling elite by commitment to the idea, not property; not stated.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism is traditionalist and rejects Western feminist and liberal ecological frames; inferred.

reification.rationale: Dugin criticises liberal commodification but this Marxist concept is not part of Eurasianist doctrine.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the view that Western liberal freedoms mask the control of money and the Atlantic bloc over the media.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian ideocratic strong state that rules by the national idea rather than liberal legal limits.

racial-franchise.rationale: Eurasianism is explicitly multi-ethnic, stressing the Slavic-Turkic symbiosis and rejecting Romano-Germanic chauvinism, so a single-group franchise is not its position.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed; the strong-state and traditionalist outlook leaves adherents without a clear view.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian, ideocratic strong state, which does not favour open records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from the Orthodox, Muslim and Buddhist cooperation in the Eurasian civilisation; marriage law was not addressed.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from the multi-confessional and multi-ethnic civilisational unity it promotes.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Classical Eurasianists favoured an authoritarian ideocratic state and Dugin a strong hierarchical one, so decision by randomly chosen citizens runs against it; inferred, not addressed directly.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Eurasianists stress Orthodoxy and traditionalism as civilisational foundations and reject Western modernising reform of the faith; inferred from that emphasis.

missingStatements.text: Ideas such as democracy and human rights are the product of one civilization, not universal values.
missingStatements.rationale: Trubetskoy called European universalism Romano-Germanic chauvinism and Dugin treats democracy and human rights as Western rather than universal.

missingStatements.text: No culture or civilization is higher or lower than another; they are only different.
missingStatements.rationale: Trubetskoy rejects the evolutionary ladder of cultures and says there is only similar and dissimilar.

missingStatements.text: The world should be divided among several great civilizational blocs rather than led by one superpower.
missingStatements.rationale: Eurasianism is built on opposition to US-led Atlanticism and the creation of a Eurasian bloc.

notes: Classical Eurasianism split into anti-Soviet and pro-Soviet currents and rejected ethnic nationalism and racial doctrines, while Dugin's version is described by critics as fascist and gives Russians priority. Economic answers are mostly inferred because the classical writers left economics undeveloped.
